# Format fixtures (C++ ↔ Rust)

The contract between the C++ formats and `rust/crates/vigil-formats` (RUST_PLAN P2,
[VALIDATION.md §8](../../../docs/VALIDATION.md)), and the C++ semantics the Rust engine stands on
(`rust/crates/vigil-detection`, P3A, [VALIDATION.md §9](../../../docs/VALIDATION.md)). Everything
here is either written by hand or generated by the C++ side; the Rust side must reproduce it byte
for byte.

| Path | Made by | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `inputs/<kind>/` | hand, and `VigilFormats generate` | Files read as `<kind>` (`json`, `trace`, `outcome`, `marks`, `profile`, `config`): real outputs (profiles of corpus players, configurations, an every-field trace, all 256 bytes in strings) and edge cases aimed at every default, clamp, bound, cast and refusal |
| `canon/<kind>/<file>` | `VigilFormats canon-all` | The C++ canonical form (parse + write) of each accepted input |
| `canon/<kind>/<file>.refused` | `VigilFormats canon-all` | The reason C++ refuses an input (Rust must refuse with the same words) |
| `numbers.txt` | `VigilFormats generate` | 4 600+ doubles (bits, and the text `core/json` writes): every number-writing regime, ties, subnormals, floats promoted to double, 1/32 positions, random bit patterns |
| `math.txt` | `VigilFormats generate` | `sin`, `cos`, `atan2`, `pow`, `sqrt`, `fmod`, `floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `fmax` on the engine's input ranges, as computed by the MSVC CRT (RUST_PLAN §8); since P3A also `powf` (the confidence gain is `std::pow(float, float)`) and `powi` (`std::pow(double, int)` in BHop and Velocity) |
| `check-catalog.json` | `VigilFormats generate` | Check and indicator ids in index order, as the C++ engine reports them |
| `hash-order.txt` | `VigilFormats generate` | P3A: the iteration order of MSVC's `std::unordered_map` (int and string keys) after random insert / erase / clear scripts through every growth step — the order in which the engine visits entities. Reproduced by `vigil_detection::hashorder` |
| `printf.txt` | `VigilFormats generate` | P3A: `snprintf` output for every conversion the engine's evidence texts, debug lines and the parity dump use, over ties, signed zeros, NaN, infinities, huge and tiny values and engine ranges. Reproduced by `vigil_detection::printf` |
| `checks.json` | `VigilFormats generate` | P3A: what each check declares beyond its parameters — name, category, summary, the "about" text, required signals, tick-sampling support, Sensitivity presets |
| `divergences.txt` | hand | Inputs on which the two sides deliberately disagree, with their classification |

Related fixtures one level up: `../engine-schema.json` and `../engine-config.default.json` (P1),
and the golden trace in `../../traces/`.

**Checks:** `VigilFormats check tests/fixtures/formats` (CTest `format_fixtures`) fails when a
committed file is not what the current C++ code produces; `cargo test` in `rust/` fails when Rust
disagrees with a committed file. Comparisons ignore `\r`, so line-ending conversion on checkout is
harmless.

**Regenerate** after an intended change (and review the diff):

```powershell
build\Release\VigilFormats.exe generate tests\fixtures\formats
build\Release\VigilFormats.exe canon-all tests\fixtures\formats
```

Inputs that would be undefined behavior in C++ (for example a negative number cast to an unsigned
id) are deliberately absent: there is no defined C++ result for Rust to match.
